mainTopic: Whether חלה and תרומה nowadays are דאורייתא; the three stages of a girl's growth and the signs of בגרות
overview: This amud finishes a discussion about whether רבי יוסי holds that תרומה in our times is a Torah obligation (דאורייתא). The גמרא tries to prove from a ברייתא that he holds it is only דרבנן, because he exempts a dough made from a rabbinic mixture of תרומה from חלה. The proof is rejected: maybe רבי יוסי holds that תרומה is דאורייתא while חלה is only דרבנן. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע backs this up from the verse 'בבואכם'. חלה is Torah law only when all of Israel is in the land, and not everyone came back with עזרא. Then a new משנה compares a girl's growth to a ripening fig in three stages: קטנה, נערה, and בוגרת. Her father has rights to what she finds, to her earnings, and to cancelling her vows until she becomes a בוגרת. The משנה and the גמרא then discuss the physical signs of בגרות, along with stories about how שמואל and other אמוראים treated their maidservants. A ברייתא listing more signs begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: a dough made from the mixture and חלה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes. According to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the dough is obligated in חלה and is not disqualified by a טבול יום. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון exempt it from חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obligated in חלה, and it is not disqualified by a טבול יום. These are the words of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון exempt it from חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that it brought as a possible proof. The ברייתא ends with a מחלוקת over whether this dough is obligated in חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dough contains תרומה that fell into a larger amount of ordinary produce. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה treat the תרומה as cancelled, so the dough counts as ordinary: it owes חלה, and a טבול יום does not disqualify it. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון exempt it from חלה because the mixture still carries a תרומה status, and תרומה does not owe חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough that must be given to a כהן
It is obligated
Someone who was impure and immersed today but must wait for nightfall to become fully pure
Becomes disqualified (unfit to eat)
They exempt

phrases.english: It is obligated in challah
and it is not disqualified by one who immersed that day,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda;
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon
exempt it from challah.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיֶּיבֶת בְּחַלָּה וְאֵינָהּ נִפְסֶלֶת בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יוסי exempts a dough made from the mixture from חלה

steps.title: The assumption that תרומה and חלה share the same status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states an assumption: whoever holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא also holds the same for חלה, and whoever holds that תרומה is דרבנן holds the same for חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that the one who says תרומה is דאורייתא holds that חלה is דאורייתא, and the one who says תרומה is דרבנן holds that חלה is דרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying down a starting assumption that ties תרומה and חלה together. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs this link because the ברייתא only tells us about חלה, but the question is about תרומה. If the two always go together, then whatever we learn about רבי יוסי's view of חלה applies to תרומה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed (a starting assumption that may later be questioned)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
A Torah-level obligation
A rabbinic-level obligation

steps.confusionAlert: The word סברוה signals an assumption, not a conclusion. Step 4 will challenge exactly this assumption.

phrases.english: They assumed: the one who says teruma is by Torah law
phrases.notes: He means תרומה nowadays, in our times.

phrases.english: holds that challah is by Torah law,
and the one who says teruma is by rabbinic law
holds that challah is by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ, מַאן דְּאָמַר תְּרוּמָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא — חַלָּה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the premise that lets the ברייתא about חלה be used to learn about תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumed premise: the status of חלה nowadays always matches the status of תרומה.

steps.title: A rabbinic mixture can only cancel a rabbinic חלה
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי holds that חלה is דרבנן, it makes sense that a mixture which is תרומה only by rabbinic law cancels the חלה obligation. A rabbinic mixture could not cancel a Torah-level חלה. So רבי יוסי must hold that חלה, and therefore תרומה, is דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say רבי יוסי holds that חלה nowadays is דרבנן, then a rabbinic mixture comes and cancels a rabbinic חלה. But if you say חלה is דאורייתא, can a rabbinic mixture come and cancel a Torah חלה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds its proof: רבי יוסי's exemption only makes sense if חלה nowadays is just rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the תרומה in the mixture is cancelled by the majority, so the mixture is תרומה only by rabbinic law. Something rabbinic cannot cancel a Torah obligation, so רבי יוסי must hold that חלה is דרבנן. Using the assumption from step 2, he would also hold that תרומה is דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say (this works out fine)
Nowadays, in the present time
A mixture of תרומה with ordinary produce
Cancels, removes an obligation
But if you say (this does not work)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic בשלמא / אלא structure: one option fits, the other leads to a difficulty, so the גמרא concludes in favor of the first option.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that Rabbi Yosei holds
that challah nowadays is by rabbinic law,
then a rabbinic mixture comes
and cancels a rabbinic challah obligation.
But if you say challah is by Torah law,
can a rabbinic mixture come
and cancel a Torah-law challah obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי חַלָּה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא (step 1) and the assumption (step 2) to build the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds תרומה nowadays is דרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי exempts a dough made from a rabbinic mixture from חלה, which only works if חלה is דרבנן

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוסי separates תרומה from חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: perhaps רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא while חלה is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps רבי יוסי holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא, and חלה is דרבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by questioning the assumption from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only showed that רבי יוסי holds חלה is דרבנן. If תרומה and חלה can have different statuses, his view on חלה tells us nothing about תרומה. He could still hold that תרומה is דאורייתא, as stated in his סדר עולם.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a rejection by offering another possibility)
He holds

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ברייתא fails: רבי יוסי may hold that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא even though חלה is only דרבנן, so the two do not have to go together.

phrases.english: But perhaps Rabbi Yosei holds:
teruma nowadays is by Torah law,
and challah is by rabbinic law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: תְּרוּמָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְחַלָּה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3 by attacking the assumption of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא regarding רבי יוסי's view on תרומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that תרומה and חלה must share the same status is not proven. רבי יוסי may treat them differently.

steps.title: The scholars of בי רב: even if תרומה is rabbinic, חלה is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its rejection with a story from רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. He heard the scholars of בי רב say that even someone who holds תרומה nowadays is דרבנן agrees that חלה is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like the reply of רב הונא son of רב יהושע. He said: I found the scholars of the house of רב sitting and saying: even according to the one who says תרומה nowadays is rabbinic, חלה is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the idea from Step 4 (תרומה and חלה can have different status) already came up in an earlier discussion. It begins by quoting the scholars of בי רב, who split the two in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 assumed that חלה and תרומה always share one status. These scholars say they can differ: תרומה can be דרבנן while חלה stays דאורייתא. Their reason comes in the next step, and רב הונא's reply comes after that.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה in our times, after the first exile
From the Torah, a Torah-level obligation
A rabbinic obligation
And like the reply that someone gave
The scholars of רב's study hall

steps.confusionAlert: The scholars of בי רב do NOT match the answer in Step 4. They split the two the other way. The part of the story that matches Step 4 is רב הונא's own reply, which comes in Step 7.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְאַהְדַּר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: And it is like the reply of Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: In other words, the answer we just gave (Step 4) is the same thing רב הונא once answered.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: for Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
I found the scholars of the house of Rav
sitting and saying:
Even according to the one who says
that teruma nowadays is rabbinic,
challa is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְאַהְדַּר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier discussion to show that the split proposed in Step 4 was already considered
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בי רב, even if תרומה nowadays is דרבנן, חלה is דאורייתא

steps.title: Proof from the fourteen years of conquest and division
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of בי רב point to history. In the seven years of conquest and the seven years of dividing the land, Israel was obligated in חלה but not in tithes. So חלה can apply even when tithes do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For during the seven years that they conquered the land, and the seven that they divided it, they were obligated in חלה but were not obligated in tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of בי רב give the reason for their claim that חלה can be Torah law even when תרומה is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the first fourteen years in ארץ ישראל, tithes and תרומה did not yet apply, but חלה already did. This shows that the חלה obligation does not depend on the תרומה obligation. So even today, when they say תרומה is only דרבנן, חלה can still be דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven years when Israel conquered the land under יהושע
The seven years when they divided the land among the tribes
Tithe, a portion of produce given away (here it goes together with תרומה)

phrases.english: For during the seven years that they conquered,
and the seven years that they divided the land —
they were obligated in challa,
but they were not obligated in tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the claim of בי רב
steps.raayaObject: That חלה can be דאורייתא even when תרומה is not
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical fact that חלה applied during the fourteen years of conquest and division, but tithes did not

steps.title: רב הונא's reply: even if תרומה is Torah law, חלה is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answered the scholars with the opposite split: even someone who says תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא can hold that חלה is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: even according to the one who says תרומה nowadays is from the Torah, חלה is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back on the scholars of בי רב and flips their split around. This is exactly the answer the גמרא gave for רבי יוסי in Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars said חלה is the 'stronger' obligation. רב הונא says it is the 'weaker' one: it can be rabbinic even when תרומה is Torah law. This is why the גמרא could say in Step 4 that רבי יוסי may hold תרומה is דאורייתא and חלה is דרבנן. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Even according to the one who holds
And I said to them, introducing the speaker's own reply

steps.whyThisMatters: This line directly supports the דחיה in Step 4, so the proof from רבי יוסי that תרומה nowadays is דרבנן falls away.

phrases.english: And I said to them:
Even according to the one who says
that teruma nowadays is from the Torah,
challa is rabbinic,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the scholars of בי רב with the reverse split
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the view of בי רב that חלה is the Torah-level obligation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חלה has its own condition for being Torah law, so it can be rabbinic even when תרומה is Torah law

steps.title: The ברייתא: חלה is Torah law only when all of Israel enters
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a ברייתא on the word 'בבואכם'. The Torah obligation of חלה starts only when all of Israel comes into the land, not when just some of them have come.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'When you come.' Might I think it starts once two or three spies entered the land? The verse says 'when you come': I meant when all of you come, not when some of you come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא proves his position from a ברייתא that explains the verse about חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links חלה to 'your coming' into the land. The ברייתא reads this as the coming of all of Israel, so a few people (like a handful of spies) entering is not enough. This sets a condition for חלה that has nothing to do with תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When you come', the verse about חלה
Spies
The verse teaches us
When all of you come
Some of you

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
If it says 'when you come',
one might think it starts from when there entered it
two or three spies?
The verse teaches: 'when you come' —
I said it about the coming of all of you,
and not the coming of some of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב הונא's claim
steps.raayaObject: That חלה is Torah law only when all of Israel is in the land
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'בבואכם' as the coming of all of Israel

steps.title: In עזרא's time not everyone came up, so חלה is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא applies the ברייתא: when עזרא brought the people back, not all of Israel came up. So nowadays חלה is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when עזרא brought them up, not all of them came up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his argument. Since only part of Israel returned with עזרא, the Torah condition for חלה was never met again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires all of Israel in the land, and the return under עזרא was only partial. So חלה nowadays is rabbinic, whatever one holds about תרומה. This confirms Step 4: רבי יוסי can hold that תרומה is דאורייתא while חלה is דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought them up (to ארץ ישראל)
Not all of them went up

steps.whatToRemember: Both בי רב and רב הונא agree that תרומה and חלה do not have to share the same status nowadays. רב הונא, using 'בבואכם = all of you', holds that חלה is rabbinic because not all of Israel returned with עזרא. That is why the proof from רבי יוסי about תרומה was rejected.

phrases.english: And when Ezra brought them up —
not all of them went up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule to the return under עזרא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because not all of Israel returned with עזרא, חלה nowadays is דרבנן even if תרומה is דאורייתא, which supports the rejection in Step 4

steps.title: The fig parable: three stages of a girl's growth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares a girl to a fig that grows in three stages: פגה, בוחל, and צמל. It defines פגה as childhood and בוחל as the years of נערות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים gave a parable about a woman: an unripe fig, a ripening fig, and a ripe fig. 'Unripe fig' means she is still a little girl. 'Ripening fig' means these are the days of her youth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It uses a fig as a picture for the three stages a girl passes through: קטנה, נערה, and בוגרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage of the fig matches a legal stage. פגה is a קטנה who has no signs of maturity yet. בוחל is a נערה who has started to mature. The third stage, צמל, is explained in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a picture used to explain something
An unripe fig; here it means a girl who is still a child (קטנה)
A ripening fig; here it means the stage of נערות
A fully ripe fig; here it means a בוגרת

phrases.english: MISHNA: The Sages gave a parable about a woman:
an unripe fig, a ripening fig, and a ripe fig.
Unripe fig: she is still a child;
ripening fig: these are the days of her youth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier discussion about חלה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl passes through three stages, compared to a fig: פגה (child), בוחל (נערה), צמל (בוגרת).

steps.title: The father's rights in each stage
steps.stepSummary: In both the פגה and בוחל stages, the father gets what she finds and what she earns, and he can cancel her vows. Once she is a צמל (בוגרת), he has no authority over her.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both of these stages they said: her father is entitled to what she finds, to what she earns, and to cancel her vows. Ripe fig: once she has become a בוגרת, her father no longer has any authority over her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now tells us why the stages matter. It lists the father's rights and says when they end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's rights cover both the קטנה and the נערה stages. The line between his authority and no authority is בגרות, the צמל stage.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost object that someone finds
Her earnings, the work of her hands
Cancelling vows
She has become a בוגרת, a fully grown woman
Authority, control

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical point of the whole parable. The stage a girl is in decides whether her father has rights over her.

phrases.english: In this stage and in that stage they said:
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the first two stages: פגה and בוחל.

phrases.english: her father is entitled to what she finds,
and to her earnings, and to cancelling her vows.
Ripe fig: once she has become fully grown,
her father no longer has authority over her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the legal results of the stages set out in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father has rights to her found objects, her earnings, and her vows while she is a קטנה or a נערה. He has none once she is a בוגרת.

steps.title: What are the signs of full maturity?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which physical signs show that a girl has reached בגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the signs?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The משנה asks for the signs of בגרות and is getting ready to list the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have just learned that בגרות ends the father's authority. So we need to know how to tell when it has arrived.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs, physical markers

phrases.english: What are the signs?
phrases.notes: He means the signs that she has reached the third stage, צמל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to recognize the stage that ends the father's authority (step 11).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical signs that show a girl has become a בוגרת.

steps.title: Four opinions on the signs of maturity
steps.stepSummary: Four תנאים give different signs of בגרות, all related to the development of the breasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: from when a fold appears under the breast. רבי עקיבא says: from when the breasts hang down. בן עזאי says: from when the area around the nipple turns dark. רבי יוסי says: when a person puts his hand on the nipple, it sinks in and is slow to come back.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question with four different opinions about which sign shows בגרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four opinions measure breast development. Each one picks a different point as the sign: a fold, hanging, darkening, or firmness that springs back slowly.

keyTerms.meaning: A fold or crease
Breast
The tip of the breast, the area around the nipple
Literally the stem of a fruit; here, the nipple

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
from when a fold appears under the breast.
Rabbi Akiva says: from when the breasts hang down.
Ben Azzai says: from when the area around the nipple darkens.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא נוֹתֵן יָדוֹ עַל הָעוֹקֶץ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: when a person places his hand on the nipple,
and it sinks in and is slow to come back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Four different signs of בגרות: a fold under the breast, hanging breasts, a darkened nipple area, or a nipple that sinks in and returns slowly.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה: פגה = קטנה, בוחל = נערה (father has rights in both), צמל = בוגרת (no rights). There are four opinions on the signs of בגרות.

steps.title: Where the word פגה comes from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from a פסוק in שיר השירים that פגה means an unripe fig.
steps.simpleTranslation: פגה means she is still a child, as it is written: 'The fig tree puts forth its green figs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining the משנה's word פגה. It brings a פסוק that uses this word for young, unripe figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the first unripe fruit a fig tree produces. That matches the girl who has not yet started to mature.

keyTerms.meaning: Put forth, began to form (fruit)
As it is written in a פסוק

phrases.english: GEMARA: Unripe fig: she is still a child,
as it is written: "The fig tree puts forth its green figs."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts explaining the words used in the משנה's parable.
steps.raayaObject: That פגה means an early, unripe fig.

steps.title: Where the word בוחל comes from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from a משנה about tithes that בוחל means a fig that has started to ripen. רב explains this as the stage when the tips of the figs turn white.
steps.simpleTranslation: בוחל means the days of youth, as we learned in a משנה: figs become obligated from when they begin to ripen. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רב: that means from when their tips turn white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word בוחל. It uses a משנה that uses the same root, plus רב's explanation of what that ripening looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in מעשרות uses the verb from בוחל for figs that are starting to ripen. רב explains that this is when their tips whiten: they are beginning to ripen but are not fully ripe yet. That matches the נערה, who is in the middle stage.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
They begin to ripen (same root as בוחל)
Turns white

phrases.english: Ripening fig: these are the days of youth,
as we learned: figs, from when they begin to ripen,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rav said:
from when their tips turn white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה's words, moving from פגה to בוחל.
steps.raayaObject: That בוחל means a fig that has started, but not finished, ripening.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעשרות 1:2, with רב's explanation through רבה בר בר חנה.

steps.title: A second פסוק for the word בוחל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another source for the meaning of בוחל, from a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, learn it from here: "My soul grew impatient with them, and their soul also grew disgusted (בָּחֲלָה) with Me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second proof for what בוחל means. This time it uses a פסוק in זכריה that has the same root, בחל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15 the proof came from a משנה about tithes. Here the גמרא shows the same root in a פסוק, where בחל describes something growing or developing. Either source supports the idea that בוחל is the middle, growing stage.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (it introduces another option)
Grew (in disgust), from the same root as בוחל

phrases.english: And if you want, say it is learned from here:
"And My soul became impatient with them,
and their soul also grew disgusted with Me."
phrases.notes: The key word is בָּחֲלָה. It shares a root with בוחל, the stage the גמרא is defining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative source for the same word that Step 15 explained
steps.raayaObject: That בוחל means a stage of growth
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 11:8, where the root בחל appears

steps.title: What the word צמל means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that צמל means 'it has come out full', which describes a fully ripe fig.
steps.simpleTranslation: צמל is like saying "it came out full."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes defining the three fig words by explaining the last one, צמל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צמל is read as a short form of יצתה מלאה, 'it came out full.' This describes the fully ripe fig. It matches the last stage, בגרות, when the father no longer has authority over his daughter (Step 11).

keyTerms.meaning: A fully ripe fig; the stage of בגרות
It came out full

phrases.english: צמל,
is like one who says: "It came out full."
phrases.notes: The word צמל is read as if it were built from the sounds of יצתה מלאה.

steps.whatToRemember: פגה is an unripe fig, בוחל is a fig starting to ripen, and צמל is a fully ripe fig. These match the three stages of a girl's growing up.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the set of three fig words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צמל means a fruit that has come out fully ripe

steps.title: שמואל explains רבי יוסי הגלילי's sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי's sign from the משנה, a fold under the breast, and שמואל explains it does not mean an actual fold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: What are the signs? רבי יוסי הגלילי says: from when a fold appears. שמואל said: it does not mean an actual fold. It means that when she stretches her hands behind her, it looks as if there is a fold under the breast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of signs of בגרות and quotes the first opinion. שמואל then explains how to understand it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה seems to require a real, lasting fold under the breast. שמואל says this is not required. It is enough that the breast has grown so much that a fold would appear when she pulls her hands back. This sets the sign at an earlier and easier-to-check point.

keyTerms.meaning: A fold or crease
Actually, literally
Breast

phrases.english: And what are the signs?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's question from Step 12, quoted again so the גמרא can explain it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From when the fold appears.
Shmuel said:
Not from when an actual fold appears,
but enough that when she stretches her hands behind her,
it looks as if a fold appears
under the breast.

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not arguing with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He is explaining what רבי יוסי הגלילי meant.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזֶהוּ סִימָנִים? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the fig words and returns to the משנה's list of signs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sign is met once a fold would appear when she stretches her hands back; a permanent fold is not needed

steps.title: שמואל checks the signs and pays for embarrassment
steps.stepSummary: שמואל checked these signs on his maidservant and then paid her four זוז for her embarrassment.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל checked his maidservant and gave her four זוז as payment for her embarrassment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. שמואל checked these signs himself on his maidservant, and he paid her because the check embarrassed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל wanted to know the signs exactly, so he checked them in real life. Even though she was his slave, he saw the check as shameful for her and paid her for it. The next step explains why he felt he had to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: His maidservant
זוזים, silver coins
Payment for her embarrassment

phrases.english: Shmuel checked on his maidservant,
and gave her four zuz
as payment for her embarrassment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about how שמואל came to know the sign he explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל paid his maidservant for the embarrassment of the check

steps.title: Why שמואל paid: slaves are for work, not shame
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל's payment follows his own teaching that slaves were given for work and not to be shamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל follows his own view, because שמואל said: "You may make them work forever" means I gave them to you for work, not for shame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the story by linking it to something שמואל taught elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A master is allowed to have his slave work for him. שמואל learns from the פסוק that this permission covers work only. It does not allow the master to shame the slave. So embarrassing his maidservant meant שמואל owed her payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning
For work
Shame, embarrassment

phrases.english: Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said:
"You may make them work forever" —
I gave them for work, and not for shame.

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a master who shames his non-Jewish slave must pay him for it.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the payment in Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves are given for work and not for shame, so shaming one requires payment

steps.title: How three אמוראים guarded their maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes how שמואל, רב נחמן and רב ששת each arranged things for their maidservants.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would assign a set partner to each maidservant. רב נחמן would switch them around. רב ששת handed them over to Arabs and told them: Be careful to stay away from Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of maidservants, the גמרא lists the different practices of three אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave each maidservant one assigned slave and did not let them choose freely. רב נחמן switched them between his slaves. רב ששת gave them over to Arabs and warned them to keep away from Jews. All three were concerned with what the maidservants did in this area, but each handled it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Assigns one specific partner
Switches, exchanges
Arabs
Be careful

phrases.english: Shmuel would assign a set partner for them,
Rav Nachman would switch them around,
Rav Sheshet handed them over to Arabs
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is how the regular printed גמרא spells it; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling.

phrases.english: and said to them: Be careful about Jews.

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל explained the sign of בגרות. His story shows that a master may make his slave work but may not shame her, and the גמרא ends with how different אמוראים guarded their maidservants.
steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל מְיַיחֵד לְהוּ, רַב נַחְמָן מַחְלֵיף לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more stories about how אמוראים treated their maidservants
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three different practices for guarding maidservants

steps.title: What does עוקץ mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יוסי's sign in the משנה and asks what the word עוקץ means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי says, etc. What is עוקץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי יוסי's statement from the משנה and asks what one word in it means. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's sign in the משנה is about pressing on the עוקץ. Before we can use the sign, we need to know which part of the body עוקץ refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally a sting or a point; here, a body part named in רבי יוסי's sign
'Etc.' The גמרא quotes only the opening words of the line from the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says, etc.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוסי's sign in the משנה: pressing a hand on the עוקץ, it sinks and is slow to come back up.

phrases.english: What is 'oketz'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about the maidservants and goes back to explaining the next sign listed in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word עוקץ in רבי יוסי's sign.

steps.title: שמואל: עוקץ is the tip of the breast
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that עוקץ means the nipple, the pointed tip of the breast.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is the point of the breast.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question: the עוקץ is the tip of the breast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יוסי's sign is clear. One presses on the nipple, and if it sinks in and is slow to come back up, she has reached בגרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Its point or tip
Breast

phrases.english: Shmuel said: The point of the breast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עוקץ is the tip of the breast, meaning the nipple.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the signs of maturity: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what the signs of בגרות are, and רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says it is when the breasts knock against each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What are the signs of maturity? רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: From when the breasts knock against each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists more opinions about the signs of בגרות. The first opinion is that the breasts have grown big enough to knock against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds new signs beyond the ones in the משנה. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's sign is about the size of the breasts.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs of full maturity (the stage after נערות)
From when they knock against each other

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן סִימָנֵי בַגְרוּת?
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: What are the signs of maturity?
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
From when the breasts knock against each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן סִימָנֵי בַגְרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with more opinions on the same topic as the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, בגרות begins when the breasts are large enough to knock against each other.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: when the tip darkens
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says the sign is when the tip of the nipple darkens.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: From when the tip of the nipple darkens.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion: בגרות begins when the tip of the nipple turns dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sign is about a change in color, not size. The גמרא is about to question it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it darkens
The tip of the protrusion (literally 'the tip of the nose'), meaning the tip of the nipple

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:
From when the tip of the protrusion darkens.
phrases.notes: חוטם usually means 'nose'. Here it is the bump in the middle of the nipple.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: מִשֶּׁיַּכְסִיף רֹאשׁ הַחוֹטֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה as first quoted, בגרות begins when the tip of the nipple darkens.

steps.title: Darkening would make her old
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that darkening comes far too late, so this sign would push בגרות into old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when it darkens? You have made her old!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's sign as it was quoted. Darkening only happens much later in life, so it cannot be the start of בגרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sign of בגרות has to show up around the time a girl actually matures. If the sign were darkening, a girl would only count as a בוגרת when she was already old, and that makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: You have made her old

phrases.english: From when it darkens?
You have made her old!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sign quoted in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's sign of darkening.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Darkening comes too late in life to mark the start of בגרות.

steps.title: רב אשי: when the tip splits
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the sign is really that the tip of the nipple splits, not that it darkens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: From when the tip of the protrusion splits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by giving a different sign: the tip of the nipple splits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that he is dropping the 'darkening' version. Splitting is something that happens at the right age, so it can mark the start of בגרות.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it splits or divides

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
From when the tip of the protrusion splits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִשֶּׁיַּפְצִיל רֹאשׁ הַחוֹטֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sign was the tip darkening, which comes too late.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sign is the tip splitting, which happens at the right time.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's sign is read as the tip of the nipple splitting, not darkening, because darkening would come only in old age.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: when a ring forms around it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the sign is when a ring forms around the nipple.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: From when a ring surrounds it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives another opinion: בגרות begins when the nipple has grown enough to be surrounded by a ring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new sign in the ברייתא, different from רבי יוסי's pressing test in the משנה. It looks at the ring that forms around the nipple.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it surrounds
The ring or circle (literally 'crown')

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רבי יוסי's sign in the משנה (Step 13, explained in Steps 22-23). That one was about pressing on the עוקץ; this one is about a ring forming around it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
From when the ring surrounds it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list of opinions after the side discussion about רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי in the ברייתא, בגרות begins when a ring forms around the nipple.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: when there is softening
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון begins his sign: from when there is a softening. His words continue after this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: From when there is a softening...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins the last opinion, רבי שמעון's. His sentence is not finished yet and continues after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's sign is about the breast becoming soft. We will only see exactly what he means once his words continue.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it is softened or pressed down

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: From when there is a softening

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון's sign has to do with a softening; it is finished after this section.
